pr_title: fix(core): Allow hybrid CD scheduling to support multiple "Angular zo…
pr_body:
…nes"

This commit updates the inside/outside NgZone detection of the hybrid CD scheduling to track the actual instance of the NgZone being used rather than the name "Angular" (how `isInsideAngularZone` works). This allows the scheduling to work correctly when there are multiple versions of Angular running on the page.

fixes #57261

issue_context.title: zone based apps + new scheduler: signal changes in another zone not triggering CD
comments:
I suspect you are seeing a really interesting "bug" here where you have two _different_ Angular Zones on the page: one in the shell application and one in Mf1.

"Hybrid mode" logic only steps in and schedules its own change detection if the notification doesn't happen in the Angular zone. In this case it _does_ happen in the zone - just not the right one. The problem is the line
https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/packages/core/src/change_detection/scheduling/zoneless_scheduling_impl.ts#L179C56-L179C67 and specifically `NgZone.isInAngularZone()` which checks that you're in _some_ Angular zone but doesn't check if it's the one for the current application. That could be easily changed, I suspect.
Fwiw, the consumer node of the reactiveLView is not marked dirty on the Zonefull MF.

@atscott @alxhub: thanks a lot for your work and the PR! I'm (unfortunately) still confused about a scenario: should hybrid mode also work among different ng-apps built separately and loaded in the same webpage? So a different setup compared to the one in the stackbliz above... If the answer is yes, I think there might be another problem affecting signals... (just signals: with observables + asyncPipe it seems to work fine). Here is an example of what I mean: - **shell**: ng-app loading zone.js (built separately), - **mf1**: zone.js based ng-app using [zone.js from the global scope](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/packages/zone.js/lib/zone.ts#L82) (mf1 built separately, bundled loaded by shell), - **mf2**: zoneless ng-app (mf2 built separately, bundled loaded by shell). This is a repro: https://github.com/mauriziocescon/mf-test. I know: no stackbliz (I need a workspace with 3 apps)! I tried anyway to make the example as easy as possible: - commands: `npm i` and then `npm run start:shell` (nothing else), - `npm run start:shell`: build mf1 and mf2 and moves the bundles to the shell public-folder, - shell loads both bundles and attaches 2 objects to the global scope (1 signal, 1 observable), - mf1 and mf2 are trying to react to shell global objects changes, - **no signal reaction in mf1 / mf2 when there are shell changes**, - **observable reaction in mf1 / mf2 when there are shell changes**. I hope I haven't done anything stupid in the code or missed an important point (don't wanna waste your time)!

This doesn't actually have to do with the hybrid scheduling. Angular doesn't have per-binding change detection so the fact that your observable binding is updating but the signal value is not means that the computed is not updating. @pkozlowski-opensource @alxhub can comment about cross-application signals/signal graphs.

As an aside, now that I think about it, I don't know that the PR totally works with the zone instance id since each application will have its own counter and end up duplicating IDs...

Hey! 

Sorry to bother you again... but I was wondering: is there any plan (even long term) to support signals-based-reactivity for cross ng-applications? See example above! 

Main use case: sharing state within a micro frontend (angular based) setup. See (for example) `https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/34377#issuecomment-2334164509`. 

Thanks a lot!

review_comments:
Wouldn't it make sense to compare the instance id prop itself, avoiding the need for the third property?

```suggestion
      Zone.current.get(angularZoneInstanceIdProperty) === this.angularZoneId
```

This doesn't quite work for two reasons:

* You could be in a child zone of the Angular zone so it might not be the exact zone you're in
* There can be two apps on the page, and one might even live within the other. The presence of a property in the hierarchy doesn't mean it's the app's Zone that you're looking for.
Oooh, that is very subtle but good points!
I meant to write a test for these cases. Let me see what I can do.
